title: Mid-run structured note-taking so interrupted tickets resume from a checkpoint
source: https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/effective-context-engineering-for-ai-agents and https://platform.claude.com/cookbook/tool-use-context-engineering-context-engineering-tools — structured note-taking + compaction as the two mechanisms for long-horizon agents; context rot degrades recall well before the hard token limit
description: The memory design is end-loaded: `_build_memory_section()` (scripts/delegate.py:1004) tells the Morty to read the role scratchpad at task START and append 'WHAT I LEARNED' at task END. Nothing is persisted mid-run, so when a long ticket is killed by the subprocess timeout, auto-compacted, or requeued by prometheus's interrupted-ticket logic (commits b8734ad / e261888), the next attempt starts from zero context and re-does the same file reads — the exact long-horizon failure mode Anthropic's context-engineering guidance addresses with per-task progress notes. The role-level scratchpad is also the wrong granularity: it mixes lessons from unrelated tickets into every prompt instead of carrying the current ticket's state.
proposed_changes: 1) Add `_ticket_progress_path(root, ticket_id)` → `.cto/scratchpad/progress/{ticket_id}.md` next to `_ensure_scratchpad()` (delegate.py:978). 2) Add a `<progress_protocol>` block to the STABLE PREFIX in build_prompt (after `<reasoning_protocol>`, delegate.py:1688): instruct the agent to OVERWRITE (never append) a ≤30-line checkpoint at that path after each of ANALYZE / PLAN / EXECUTE / SELF_CRITIQUE, with exactly four sections — `PHASE:`, `DONE:` (files already changed, with what changed), `NEXT:` (the single next action), `UNKNOWNS:` — and to treat the file as the source of truth over its own recollection. Overwrite-not-append keeps the injected context bounded. 3) In the VOLATILE SUFFIX, when the progress file exists and is non-empty, inject it as `<resumed_progress>` (truncate to ~2000 chars) immediately before the mission block with the directive 'A previous attempt at THIS ticket was interrupted. Verify each DONE item with Read/Grep before trusting it, then continue from NEXT — do not restart from scratch.' 4) Wire cleanup: delete the progress file when a ticket reaches a terminal status in scripts/ticket.py's status-update path, so a reopened ticket never inherits stale state. 5) Do not inject `<resumed_progress>` on first attempt (attempt counter / retry_count == 0) to keep the cold-start prompt unchanged.
